Nobody will care about this, but in the section

The Latin was found to be a series of sentences showing different conjugations of the verb Vendo, to sell.

it should be "the verb Vendere", as that is the proper infinitive form in Latin, the one used to identify a verb.

item.title: Re: Words
item.content:encoded: I agree a little bit, but to me it just read like a one-sided audio log. Definitely could be cleaned up or have the rest of the crew's conversation added

item.title: Re: Words
item.content:encoded: I have to agree, I was thinking the exact same thing while reading through this. I like the content for the story, but the writing structure is almost irritating. I was very aware the whole time that I was reading a written tale and not a transcript of an audio log.

item.title: Words
item.content:encoded:
"All right, I'm walking into the lobby. Walls are mostly bare concrete, a little paint here and there. Graffiti everywhere. A few beer bottles, some other trash. Looks like just another abandoned building.

"Okay, I'm making my way up the stairs. More graffiti on the walls. Okay, I'm going into the hallway.

Sorry, I didn't get to read 4 lines before I had to point something out :p And if it stops me from immersing myself and enjoying the read, you might take it into consideration as others will, too.

Anyways. Please remove at least one of the "All right"/"Okay"/"Okay". Sounds like the guy had a stroke :P
If his/her reason for repeating the same words is because he's/she's answering affirmative to someone, I think you should rather make a new line entirely.

Otherwise I enjoy this so far.

Edit:

Okay, here's a classroom. Pretty empty. Some old desks. Real old, like they had in the thirties. The chalkboard's got a few math problems on it. Looks like trig. Okay, I'm going to check out another room.

Come on, man.

OK so I skimmed through the rest, it's unreadeable for me.
Sorry, but this is horrible structuring and an unrestricted usage of the ONE word "Okay". Okay I thought at least you would vary the words, okay?

Seriously though, this may be a great story but I can't force myself to read the rest.. if you'd remove 3/4 of the "Okay"'s and use proper quotation in the monologue that would fix it for me at least.
